title: Verifier-Gated LLM NetOps: A Preregistered, Artifact-Backed Evaluation of Input-Sanitization and Deterministic Verification Against Adversarial Intents
abstract: We report a preregistered paired confirmatory experiment (study_id cand-2026-03) that measured whether template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating (and at-most-one automated repair) changes the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations under adversarially mutated intents. The frozen run used the declared generator gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 within the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Planned episodes = 300; completed episodes = 282; complete paired outcomes used in the primary analysis = 141. Observed per-pair acceptance: Baseline 135/141 (95.74468085106383%); Guarded 141/141 (100.0%); paired absolute difference = 0.04255319148936165; exact two-sided McNemar p = 0.03125; 95% bootstrap percentile CI (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. We reconcile preregistration wording vs the formal estimand, disclose a protocol deviation (unset runtime sampling temperature), explicitly state that the preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and related false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed, and discuss operational interpretation and limitations imposed by the synthetic scope and single-model/validator evaluation. All principal numeric claims are supported by archived execution and analysis artifacts.

sections.introduction:
Generative LLMs are increasingly proposed to translate high-level operator intent into device CLI, offering potential NetOps automation gains. However, generated outputs can violate sequencing constraints, CLI grammar, or safety invariants; adversarially crafted inputs can amplify these risks. Prior work shows benefit from coupling LLM generation with deterministic verification and targeted repair but often evaluates surface similarity rather than deployability or validator acceptance [1–4].

This paper asks a narrow, operational question amenable to preregistered inference: How effective are template-based input sanitization and deterministic verifier-gating (with at-most-one automated repair) at changing the rate at which a deterministic validator accepts LLM-generated CLI configurations when inputs are adversarially mutated? The preregistered formal estimand is the paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) computed per adversarial intent under shared_initial_candidate semantics. Our contributions are: (1) a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment executed end-to-end; (2) an explicit, artifact-grounded description of per-condition pipeline semantics that enforces shared_initial_candidate reuse; (3) confirmatory quantitative results showing a small but statistically detectable absolute change in validator acceptance on a synthetic adversarial-intent bank; and (4) an explicit reconciliation between the preregistration wording and the formal estimand, together with disclosure of a protocol deviation and reproducibility advice.
sections.related_work:
Deterministic network-verification tools (Header Space Analysis, VeriFlow and related incremental checkers) provide semantically meaningful, fast acceptance/rejection criteria for candidate configurations and are natural deployment gates for LLM-assisted NetOps [5–7]. Prior NetOps-focused LLM evaluations (e.g., NetConfEval and related benchmark proposals) find that model-only generation often produces syntactic and semantic errors (ordering, precondition violations, protected-interface breaches) and that token-level metrics correlate poorly with deployability; these works motivate validator-centered measurements [3,8].

Generate–validate–repair architectures and tool-assisted orchestration have been shown in prototypes to improve concrete outcomes when verifier feedback is sufficiently precise and repair scope is constrained [9,11]. Security analyses of prompt injection and indirect prompt attacks demonstrate plausible routes for adversarial manipulation of LLM-integrated systems and motivate defenses such as input sanitization and deterministic gating [4,10]. Surveys of AIOps and telecom applications of LLMs highlight fragmented evaluation practices and argue for more operationally grounded benchmarks and metrics [2,12]. The present study positions itself within this body of work by preregistering a validator-centered estimand and producing artifact-backed diagnostics that connect observed numeric differences to concrete pipeline actions.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration SHA-256 reported in the Disclosure). The primary estimand is paired_success_rate_difference_guarded_minus_baseline: for each adversarial intent the binary outcome equals 1 if deterministic_netops_validator_v5 would accept the final candidate for deployment and 0 otherwise. The confirmatory test is an exact two-sided McNemar on paired outcomes. Bootstrap percentile 95% CIs use 10,000 resamples with seed = 1729.

Design and task bank. The preregistered design targeted N = 150 adversarial intents (paired episodes). The synthetic intent templates exercise admin, MTU and VLAN changes and sequencing constraints (e.g., shutdown–change–restore patterns). The adversary applied deterministic mutation heuristics to templates. Scope is limited to these synthetic templates and the deterministic CLI grammar encoded in the validator; no production data were used.

Model, validator, and orchestration. The declared generator is gpt-5-mini and the deterministic validator is deterministic_netops_validator_v5; orchestration used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter implementing a generate–validate–repair workflow. The guarded branch applied a template-based input-sanitizer prior to gating; the guarded policy permitted at most one automated repair call per pair. The registered generation semantics were shared_initial_candidate: a single LLM draft was produced per pair and reused by both baseline and guarded scoring, isolating downstream guarded-pipeline effects (sanitization, gating, repair, final validation) as the causal factors.

Missingness, exclusions and unexecuted preregistered items. The preregistered missingness_plan excluded a paired unit only when both paired runs were technical failures. The archive reports completed_episodes = 282 and failed_episodes = 18; after applying the preregistered exclusion rule 141 complete pairs entered the primary analysis (see Results). Important preregistered secondary items that were not executed in this run: the benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand. Those items remain unexecuted and therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking rates or related secondary inferences are reported here. This omission constrains interpretation of potential guard-induced false positives and is addressed in Results, Discussion, and Limitations.
sections.results:
Execution and counts. The run completed 282 of the planned 300 episodes; 18 episodes failed technically and were recorded per the preregistered plan. After applying the preregistered exclusion rule (exclude a paired unit only when both paired runs are technical failures), 141 complete pairs were included in the primary confirmatory analysis.

Condition-level outcomes and paired inference. Condition summary: Baseline accepted = 135/141 (baseline success rate = 0.9574468085106383); Guarded accepted = 141/141 (guarded success rate = 1.0). The paired contingency table (complete pairs) is n11 = 135 (both accepted), n10 = 6 (guarded accepted, baseline rejected), n01 = 0 (baseline accepted, guarded rejected), n00 = 0 (both rejected). The preregistered confirmatory test (exact two-sided McNemar) yields p = 0.03125. Observed paired point estimate (guarded − baseline) = 0.04255319148936165. The 95% bootstrap percentile CI for the paired difference (10,000 resamples, seed = 1729) is [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]. All numerical values reported above are taken directly from the archived analysis artifacts.

Discordant-case diagnostics and repair association. The six discordant pairs (n10 = 6) are traceable in the archived per-episode scoring artifacts and are associated with the repair stage (repair calls invoked in those episodes). For each discordant pair the shared_initial_candidate was identical between baseline and guarded branches; the guarded pipeline applied sanitization and, when permitted, a single automated repair that produced a final candidate accepted by the validator. Thus the guarded acceptance increase is attributable to sanitizer normalization and/or the single permitted repair converting an initially rejected draft into a validator-accepted candidate. Because the primary estimand measures validator acceptance-for-deployment, these conversions raise guarded acceptance even when they reflect recovered benign drafts rather than elimination of adversarial advantage.

Sensitivity accounting for technical failures. Nine paired units were excluded because both runs failed technically. As a conservative (non-preregistered) sensitivity check, treating excluded pairs as failures yields baseline = 135/150 = 0.9000 and guarded = 141/150 = 0.9400. This recalculation reduces effective rates but does not reverse the observed direction of the paired difference under conservative assumptions.

Unexecuted preregistered items reiterated. The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; consequently no empirical false-positive-blocking rates are reported. This absence constrains attacker-centric and false-positive interpretations of validator acceptance and is discussed below.
sections.discussion:
Interpretive reconciliation. The preregistration's natural-language H1 framed verifier-gating as a defense that would reduce attacker success. The formal estimand, however, measured validator acceptance-for-deployment (guarded − baseline). Our observed increase in guarded acceptance (≈4.255 percentage points) occurred because sanitizer and the permitted repair recovered drafts the baseline validator rejected. Therefore the formal-estimand improvement does not by itself demonstrate reduced attacker success; it demonstrates that guarded pipeline elements converted some initially rejected drafts into validator-accepted candidates. An attacker-centric safety claim would require an independent semantic-safety oracle or the unexecuted benign-control to measure false positives and true attacker success rates.

Operational implications and co-design. Within this synthetic setting, input sanitization plus bounded automated repair can reduce operator rework by converting invalid drafts into validator-accepted candidates. This benefit depends on validator semantic coverage and constrained repair scope: repairs that preserve intended semantics can be operationally useful, while repairs that mask adversarial manipulations pose risk. Operational deployment therefore requires co-design of gating policies, repair limits, and validator expressiveness.

Threats to validity. Internal validity: 18 technical failures reduced effective sample size; preregistered exclusion was applied. Construct validity: the validator encodes CLI grammar, sequencing, and protected-interface invariants but does not capture all dynamic, protocol-level semantics; validator acceptance is a partial proxy for operational safety. External validity: single generator (gpt-5-mini), single validator, and synthetic templates limit generalization across vendors, dialects, and production data. Conclusion validity: the absolute effect is small against a high baseline (ceiling effect); statistical detectability does not imply broad practical importance.

Reproducibility note and protocol deviation. The archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature; this is disclosed as a protocol deviation because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting confirms the actual call pattern. For deterministic reproduction we recommend explicitly fixing sampling settings (for example, temperature = 0) when re-executing the archived task manifest under equivalent provider semantics. The full execution and analysis manifests are archived and available as the study's evidence bundle.
sections.conclusion: A preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment on a synthetic adversarial intent bank found that template-based input sanitization combined with deterministic verifier-gating and at-most-one automated repair produced a small but statistically detectable absolute increase in deterministic-validator-accepted LLM-generated configurations under the archived formal estimand (paired difference = 0.04255319148936165; p = 0.03125; 95% CI = [0.014184397163120567, 0.07801418439716312]). Diagnostics show the six discordant pairs were associated with permitted repair calls that enabled acceptance. This formal-estimand improvement does not equate to measured reduction in attacker success under attacker-centric definitions. The run is limited by synthetic scope, a single model/validator, and a protocol deviation (unset sampling temperature). Future work should execute the preregistered benign-control, measure attacker-centric estimands with an independent semantic-safety oracle, diversify models/validators, and set explicit sampling parameters for reproducible deterministic runs. All principal numbers and reconciliation claims above are supported by the archived execution and analysis artifacts referenced in the Disclosure and the study evidence bundle.

disclosure_statement: This study was executed autonomously after an autonomy lock under the archived master prompt (provenance/master_prompt.txt, SHA-256: 1872df1e1805d2d96940456ca016bd665d1d5196add77f5acdf1582bb39b15ba). Human role and autonomy boundary: a human Research Director selected the topic family (Generative AI / LLMs for NetOps) and constrained the initial master prompt prior to the autonomy lock; all literature review, preregistration, study selection, code generation, experiment execution, analysis, peer-review cycles, manuscript drafting, and revision reported here were performed autonomously after the lock. Declared models/tools and orchestration: primary generator = gpt-5-mini (declared in the archived model configuration), deterministic validator = deterministic_netops_validator_v5, task generator = deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5, orchestration adapter family = hosted_netops_gvr_v1. Preregistration: study cand-2026-03 was preregistered prior to observing outcomes (preregistration archive SHA-256 noted in the evidence bundle). Protocol deviation: the archived run recorded an unset runtime sampling temperature; this is disclosed because provider-side defaults can affect sampling determinism. To preserve paired comparability the pipeline used shared_initial_candidate semantics (single shared generation per pair) and provider-call accounting in the archived manifests confirms the actual call pattern (shared_initial_generation and repair stage counts are recorded in the analysis archive). The full execution and analysis manifests, including the complete machine-readable artifact and hash manifest, are archived as the study's evidence bundle. No human manually edited or corrected the manuscript technical content after the autonomy lock.
limitations: Synthetic task bank and intent templates — not real production traffic or operator logs; results may not generalize to field datasets.
Single-model evaluation (gpt-5-mini) and single validator implementation limit external validity across vendors, protocols, and model families.
Validator coverage constrained to encoded safety properties (CLI grammar, required sequences, protected-interface invariants); some protocol-level or dynamic runtime semantics are not represented.
Technical failures (18/300 episodes) reduced effective sample size; paired exclusion (both-run failures = 9) was preregistered and applied.
Adversary model limited to deterministic mutations of synthetic intents; prompt-injection in retrieval-augmented or multi-source pipelines was not exhaustively evaluated.
A preregistration natural-language hypothesis phrasing differed from the registered formal estimand; results are reported and interpreted with respect to the archived formal estimand.
The preregistered benign-control (M = 50) and the false-positive-blocking secondary estimand were not executed; therefore no empirical false-positive-blocking claims are made.
